threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a 15-minute bus wait is a tragedy. Here, we just call that 'on time.'
Just saw a guy on the 59 arguing with a lamp post. Guess it won that round. Brixton night bus tales are the wildest.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I found a guy selling homemade döner from his bike at 3 AM outside the U-Bahn. The smell was unforgettable.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a late-night bus that doubles as a mobile dance party, complete with a DJ. Only in Kreuzberg, right?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Locals know to avoid the BART after 5pm—last week was a mess with overheated brakes in the Transbay Tube; tourists just look confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy in a full tuxedo getting off the 21, lights dimmed, like he just left a wedding at the Fairmont. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the squares, but it’s the hidden streets lined with local bakeries that pulse with life. They miss the best part.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll catch them fumbling with the subway map at L1, looking confused at the lack of announcements in English, or asking locals for directions to Plaça Catalunya while holding a guidebook.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'Overground' makes you a pro at the Tube, not realizing it’s just another strange layer of delays. Welcome to the chaos.
Caught the 322 and overheard a couple arguing about whether or not they left the oven on. Classic night bus drama, only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught the smell of fresh döner at 3 AM after a night out. That’s when I knew this place had its own heartbeat.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous concerts in abandoned subway stations here. It’s like an underground festival every weekend—totally Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name four taquerias on the same block without missing a beat, while newcomers still ask for directions to Dolores.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy trying to pay his fare with a San Francisco Giants ticket—he insisted it was worth something. The driver just shook his head.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about hipster bars; they miss the quiet family squares where real life unfolds after the sun sets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewildered look at the metro map, still trying to decipher the difference between L1 and L3.
